item.note:
Filed 2026-05-09. Research evidence collected via web search same day:

Path #1 — Stay status quo. Local CLI (whisper/whisper-cli on PATH) + cloud HTTP fallback (Groq free tier, OpenAI). User installs local binary OR accepts cloud. Currently shipped.

Path #2 — Take the cgo hit. Switch to a build-tag-gated STT path (e.g. stt_cgo) that integrates sherpa-onnx-go-linux (best engineered option). Single-static-binary promise becomes 'single static binary except STT-using builds.' Loses the Termux/Windows-without-extra-tooling appeal but gains real local STT.

Path #3 — Bet on WASI. Productionize the whisper.cpp → WASI → wazero path. Pure Go, stays in binary. ~5x slower than native (90s vs 17s for the same audio), needs model file distribution (~75MB-1.5GB), no thread support in wazero. Months of work, untested in production by anyone in the Go ecosystem today.

Path #4 — Wait + monitor. Track Go STT ecosystem; revisit when a real pure-Go option lands. Document the constraint publicly so users understand the tradeoff.

Groq free tier (path #1 sub-option) was wired 2026-05-09 in the row 'Telegram voice STT HTTP-provider fallback' so users have a no-install option today even without resolving this row.

---

DECISION 2026-05-09: Path #3 (WASI productionization) selected.

Rationale (stakeholder): wazero gives the cleanest pure-Go deployment path; CGO_ENABLED=0 stays preserved end-to-end; the perf gap vs native whisper.cpp is acknowledged and accepted as the tradeoff for keeping the single-static-binary promise.
